Command Hierarchy Definition
Define the command tree structure below. Each command can have:
- name:        The exact word typed by the user
- abbrev:      Optional shortcut (e.g. 'sh' for 'show')
- short_desc:  Help text displayed for '?'
- activation:  The shell command executed (can use ${AETHERCLI_SCRIPTS_DIR})
- syntax:      Full syntax description shown in help
- args:        'append' to pass trailing arguments to the shell command
- admin_only:  true to restrict execution strictly to the 'admin' user
- effect:      'read', 'write' (default), or 'destructive'
- idempotent:  true if calling with same args has no additional effect (default: false)
- open_world:  true if command interacts with external environment (default: true)
- timeout_s:   Timeout in seconds for execution (e.g. 30)
- max_output_bytes: Output limit in bytes; truncates if exceeded (e.g. 65536)
- cwd:         Working directory for the subprocess
- env:         Key-value map of environment variables passed to the subprocess
- params:      Typed parameters array (name, type, description, required, enum, minimum, maximum)
- subcommands: Array of nested subcommands
